text.p: Thailand voted in a general election on Sunday. Here are some key facts about the country and the vote:
-- Thailand is a constitutional monarchy with an elected government and parliament. It covers an area of 513,115 sq km (191,113 sq miles) with a population of about 60 million people.
-- The size of its economy in terms of 1995 gross domestic product is 2.92 trillion baht (US$116.75 billion). The economy grew 8.5 percent in 1995.
-- It is the only country in Southeast Asia that has never been colonised.

-- Thailand has had 17 coups or attempted coups since 1932 when it abandoned absolute monarchy. The last coup was in February 1991, when the army overthrew the government led by prime minister Chatichai Choonhavan.
Here are some facts about the November 17 election:
-- Called by Chart Thai Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa on September 27, five days after he was forced to resign following a bruising no-confidence debate in parliament.

-- A total of 2,310 candidates (1,950 male and 360 female) from 13 parties are vying for 393 seats in parliament. There are two more parliamentary seats than in the last election due to an increase in population.
-- Eligible voters total 38 million, 200,000 more than in the last election.

-- The last election was on July 2, 1995. Chart Thai party leader Banharn Silpa-archa won the largest number of seats, beating the incumbent prime minister Chuan Leekpai, the head of the Democrat Party. Banharn quickly formed a seven-party coalition government. One coalition partner pulled out from the government in August 1996 leaving the ruling coalition with a total of 209 seats in the 391-seat House of Representatives.
On September 27 Banharn dissolved parliament and called fresh elections after coalition partners forced him to resign in return for support in a no-confidence vote.
-- Most opinion polls show Chuan's Democrat Party and Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's New Aspiration Party (NAP) running neck and neck in a tight race for the November 17 election.

But the respected Rajabhat Institute of teacher's training, whose polls have been quite accurate in previous polls, has to the surprise of many analysts put the Democrats well ahead with 149 seats against 114 for the NAP.
